records.author: Contributor 03
records.title: Calibration notes
records.body: Three Saturday observing nights lost time to mirror alignment faults. I own instrument safety. Contributor 01 agreed to investigate a repeatable alignment routine; I did not delegate safety approval.

records.author: Contributor 01
records.title: February calendar
records.body: Starting next month, Contributor 02 will handle the Saturday night rota. I will focus on the mirror-calibration checklist instead of staffing every session. This is the proposed split; we have not tried it yet.

records.author: Contributor 01
records.title: Alignment checklist revision
records.body: I wrote a checklist separating warm-up, mirror adjustment and the safety sign-off. Contributor 03 requested a stop condition for drifting measurements, and I added it. I chose a manual checklist before an automatic controller so volunteers could inspect each step.

records.author: Contributor 02
records.title: Controller experiment
records.body: Contributor 02 implemented the measurement logger. Contributor 01 tested the automatic alignment prototype during a cloudy rehearsal and reported unstable readings. Contributor 03 retained safety approval. The code merged into the experiment branch, not the public observing setup.

records.author: Contributor 01
records.title: Rehearsal decision
records.body: I stopped the automatic alignment trial after the cloudy rehearsal. We kept Contributor 02's logger and the manual checklist. I asked for a second operator to sign the stop-condition check; no repeat trial has been scheduled.

records.author: Contributor 02
records.title: April rota review
records.body: I managed the rota for three April weekends. Contributor 01 still covered April 20 when a volunteer cancelled. The change reduced their scheduled rota duties; it did not eliminate their operational involvement.

records.author: Contributor 04
records.title: Checklist at another dome
records.body: I used Contributor 01's checklist at the east dome on two evenings. The stop condition caught a drifting measurement and we postponed the session. I needed help interpreting one warm-up step. This is my report of use, not a comparative safety or speed study.

records.author: Contributor 01
records.title: End-of-season reflection
records.body: I used to judge my contribution by how many nights I personally covered. The useful change was making the steps visible to another operator. I still need to improve the warm-up wording; another person using a draft does not make the whole procedure dependable.
